chains.title: No TF-mediated allelic effect; the association is explained by linkage, pleiotropy or a bystander regulatory variant
predictions: No reproducible allele-specific ZNF687 occupancy or enhancer activity should be detected at this exact base in the disease-relevant cell type.
The cleft-lip association should be attributable to a linked causal variant, pleiotropy, or nearby regulatory variation rather than this A>G change.
The ZNF687 ChIP peak in GM12878 should not be allele-specific or relevant to craniofacial epithelium.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ZNF687 binding and enhancer activity are demonstrated at this base in craniofacial cells.
The A allele reproducibly alters IRF6 or UTP25 expression in a disease-relevant cell type.
Fine-mapping excludes linked variants and supports this position as the causal regulatory change.

chains.title: ZNF687 binding at the IRF6 dELS is a candidate activator of IRF6 in craniofacial epithelium

links.claim: ZNF687 is the only ENCODE-bound, expressed TF with a binding model reported at this variant (E04), but its only containing peak is in GM12878, not a craniofacial sample (E05), and no ZNF687 QBiC-SELEX model is supplied. The ref-A > alt-G direction is therefore not directly measured; I set ref more because the IRF6 eQTL shows alt G lowering IRF6 (E08), which is consistent with a ref-bound activator, but this is an assumption.
The variant lies in EH38E2863563, a distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal at the IRF6 locus; the signal values are biosample maxima and not craniofacial-specific.

IRF6 is 9.7 kb away, although ENSG00000289700 is also listed at 9.7 kb, so IRF6 is not uniquely nearest. E08 reports IRF6 eQTLs in brain cerebellum/hemisphere with alt G NES -0.62 and -0.61, i.e. A is associated with higher IRF6, but not in craniofacial epithelium.

The cleft-lip GWAS and cleft literature point to craniofacial epithelial biology, but no expression context was provided and the E12 lookup for keratinocyte failed, so this cell type is inferred rather than measured.

The orofacial cleft GWAS reports an association at this variant with effect allele A (p 2.0e-06); if A increases ZNF687-driven IRF6 expression in craniofacial epithelium, altered IRF6 dosage could contribute, but the mechanism is not demonstrated.

predictions: ZNF687 should bind the ref A allele more strongly than the alt G allele at this base in an allele-specific binding assay.
EH38E2863563 should show allele-dependent enhancer activity in craniofacial epithelial cells, with the A allele increasing activity if ZNF687 activates IRF6.
The A allele should associate with higher IRF6 expression in a craniofacial-relevant context, matching the direction of the brain IRF6 eQTL.
falsified_if: ZNF687 does not bind this site allele-specifically, or binds the alt G allele more strongly than ref A.
The A allele reduces rather than increases IRF6 enhancer activity or IRF6 expression in craniofacial epithelial cells.
EH38E2863563 does not contact or regulate the IRF6 promoter in craniofacial cells.

chains.title: ZNF687 binding at the same dELS regulates UTP25 and contributes to cleft lip

links.claim: ZNF687 is the only ENCODE-bound, expressed TF with a binding model at this variant (E04), but its containing peak is only in GM12878 (E05) and no ZNF687 QBiC-SELEX model is supplied. The ref-A > alt-G direction is not measured and is inferred by analogy to H1 rather than from UTP25 allele-specific data.
The variant lies in EH38E2863563, a dELS whose SCREEN nearby genes include UTP25 as well as IRF6; this is proximity-based and does not establish UTP25 as the target.

UTP25 is 12.0 kb from the variant and has the best L2G score across credible sets (0.75), but the relevant credible-set PIPs are low (0.05-0.10) and the source set for 0.75 is unspecified. Open Targets gives UTP25 a cleft-lip score of 0.35, genetic association 0.57, while E08 contains no UTP25 eQTL.

UTP25 cleft-lip literature hits and the Open Targets association support a disease link, but they do not establish UTP25 expression or function in craniofacial epithelium; no expression or chromatin-contact data are provided, and the E12 keratinocyte lookup failed.

If the A allele increases ZNF687-driven UTP25 expression in craniofacial epithelium, altered UTP25 dosage could contribute to the orofacial cleft association, but UTP25 mediation is not shown and the cleft GWAS signal is modest.

predictions: Chromatin contact or reporter assays should link EH38E2863563 to the UTP25 promoter in craniofacial cells.
The A allele should increase UTP25 expression in a craniofacial-relevant context.
UTP25, rather than IRF6, should show the stronger allele-specific regulatory effect in the disease-relevant cell type.
falsified_if: EH38E2863563 does not contact the UTP25 promoter in craniofacial cells.
The variant has no allele-specific effect on UTP25 expression.
UTP25 is not expressed or required in the relevant craniofacial epithelium.

grades_v0.reason: No evidence IDs are cited, and no TFAP2A ChIP-seq, QBiC-SELEX, or allele-specific binding assay is supplied. E04 lists only ZNF687 as a bound, expressed TF with a model in coverage; TFAP2A is absent. The ref>A direction is unsupported.

E01 and E03 directly place the variant in EH38E2863563 / ENSR1_B3JM9C, a dELS with DNase and H3K27ac signal. Caveats: the z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not craniofacial-specific, and GERP 0.516 is only modest conservation.

E02 gives IRF6 at 9.7 kb but ENSG00000289700 is at the same distance, so 'nearest' is not unique. E08 provides an IRF6 eQTL, but only in brain cerebellum/hemisphere, not craniofacial epithelium. The direction (alt G lowers IRF6, so A raises IRF6) agrees with H1, contradicting H1's own prediction wording about an 'opposite' GTEx direction.

E06 provides a cleft-lip GWAS association and E09 provides cleft-related literature hit titles, but no expression, chromatin, or functional data in craniofacial epithelial cells. The chain itself admits the cell type is inferred, not measured.

E06 directly reports an orofacial cleft association at this variant with effect allele A (p 2.0e-06). The association is modest and the IRF6-dosage mechanism is not demonstrated, but the genetic association claim itself is supported.
Same as H1.binding: no evidence IDs, no TFAP2A ChIP-seq or QBiC-SELEX, and TFAP2A is not in the covered bound-factor list in E04. The ref>A binding direction is unsupported.

E03 directly lists UTP25 among the SCREEN nearby genes for EH38E2863563, and E01/E03 place the variant in that dELS. However, 'possible target' is proximity-based only; no contact or reporter evidence links the element to UTP25.

E07 gives UTP25 an L2G score of 0.75, but the relevant credible-set PIPs are low (0.05-0.10) and the source set for 0.75 is unspecified. E09 is only a literature-search hit list for 'UTP25 AND cleft lip'; no quoted evidence shows UTP25 causality. E08 contains no UTP25 eQTL.

E09 shows cleft-lip literature hits from a UTP25 query, but the titles do not establish UTP25 expression or function in craniofacial epithelium. No expression or chromatin-contact data in a craniofacial cell type are provided.

E06 supports a cleft-lip association at the variant, but UTP25 mediation is not shown. The claim is explicitly conditional and speculative, and E09 does not provide UTP25 functional or dosage evidence.

grades_final.reason: E01/E03 directly place the variant in EH38E2863563, a distal enhancer-like cCRE, and E03 lists IRF6 among nearby genes; the claim correctly notes the signal values are biosample maxima and not craniofacial-specific.

E02 supports the 9.7 kb distance and the co-located ENSG00000289700 caveat. E08 gives IRF6 eQTLs only in brain tissues, not craniofacial epithelium, so IRF6 as the target of this element in the proposed cell type is indirect.

Cleft GWAS/literature can be read as consistent with craniofacial epithelial biology, but no expression context is supplied and the keratinocyte lookup failed; the cell type is inferred, not measured.

E06 directly reports an orofacial cleft association at this variant with effect allele A, but the proposed ZNF687-driven IRF6 mechanism and altered IRF6 dosage are explicitly not demonstrated; only a weak phenotype/mechanism link is supported.
ZNF687 occupancy is reported only in GM12878, not craniofacial epithelium, and there is no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding evidence. The ref-more direction is inferred by analogy, not measured.

E01/E03 support that the variant lies in EH38E2863563 dELS and that SCREEN lists UTP25 among nearby genes; the claim appropriately notes this is proximity-based and does not establish UTP25 as the target.

E07 supports a best L2G score for UTP25 but with low credible-set PIPs and an unspecified source set; E11 supports a UTP25 cleft-lip genetic association, but there is no UTP25 eQTL or contact evidence tying this variant to UTP25.

UTP25 cleft-lip literature and Open Targets association are consistent with disease relevance, but they do not establish UTP25 expression or function in craniofacial epithelium, and the keratinocyte lookup failed.
The variant is associated with orofacial cleft in E06, and E09/E11 support a UTP25 disease link, but UTP25 mediation of this variant's phenotype is not shown and the cleft GWAS signal is modest.

checks.why: Directly tests whether TFAP2A occupies this exact variant in a craniofacial-relevant epithelial biosample; a negative result would collapse both H1 and H2 binding links and strengthen H3.
Tests whether UTP25 has any Open Targets disease association with cleft lip, which is the main distinguishing claim of H2; absence would weaken H2.gene and H2.phenotype.
Checks whether TFAP2A is expressed in a craniofacial-relevant epithelial context, resolving the inferred cell-type link in both H1 and H2.

No ZNF687 occupancy at this element in craniofacial epithelial cells; supports the null.

The A allele increases UTP25 expression, with little or no IRF6 effect.

next_experiment: Run the cheapest discriminating assay: allele-specific ZNF687 binding at chr1:209815925 (EMSA with recombinant ZNF687, or ChIP-qPCR in a heterozygous ZNF687-expressing line) comparing ref-A and alt-G oligos. Ref-A binding more strongly supports H1; no reproducible allele-specific binding supports H3.
